iut_type: Internal QA check: a customer-submitted proxy registration content confirmation form that merely duplicates an existing prior registration's content, rather than reflecting the actually-intended new registration, must be flagged and clarified before processing
customer_question: (Internal, not a direct customer question) I believe the proxy registration content confirmation form I filled out corresponds to fields in my company's existing DID registration -- could you tell me which item in the form maps to which item in that existing registration?
question_variants: What should a consultant do if a customer's submitted registration form appears identical to an already-existing registration rather than reflecting the new design being registered?
How can a consultant detect that a customer may have misunderstood what content a registration confirmation form was supposed to capture?
actual_issue: The customer submitted a proxy registration content confirmation form whose content turned out to be effectively identical to their existing prior registration (for the IM-100 module's Controller Subsystem), rather than reflecting the actual new registration combination under discussion -- and asked which form fields corresponded to which fields in that existing registration, prompting the consultant to realize internally that he could not tell what the customer actually intended to register, since literally processing the form as submitted would not have produced anything new.
plain_english_explanation: When a customer fills out and returns a proxy registration content confirmation form, the consultant should not assume the form accurately reflects the new registration actually being discussed -- customers can mistakenly submit content that duplicates an existing, already-completed registration (in this case, by referencing the same fields as their existing IM-100 module's Controller Subsystem registration) rather than the new combination being negotiated. When this happens, the consultant should flag the discrepancy internally and seek clarification on the customer's actual intent before proceeding, rather than processing the form literally, since doing so could result in an unintended duplicate registration that does not reflect what the customer actually wants certified.
consultant_answer: (Internal note, not sent to the customer as-is) The submitted proxy registration content confirmation form is equivalent in content to the existing IM-100 registration -- I can't imagine the customer actually wants to register with this exact content, and I have no idea what they're actually hoping for. Do you understand what the customer's intent is here?
decision_logic: When a customer-submitted registration confirmation form's content appears to merely replicate an existing prior registration rather than reflecting the new design or combination under discussion, treat this as a red flag requiring internal clarification before proceeding, rather than processing the form as submitted.
final_recommendation: Build a sanity check into the proxy registration intake process that compares a newly-submitted registration confirmation form against the customer's existing registrations, and proactively flag and clarify with the customer (or internally between consultants) any case where the new form appears to simply duplicate prior registration content, before advancing the form into the actual registration workflow.
risk_if_done_wrong: Processing a registration confirmation form literally without checking whether its content actually reflects the new registration intent could result in submitting an unintended duplicate registration, wasting registration fees and requiring rework to correct.
